audit.why: HARD at 8/10 with a 48.17% win rate over 1,422 games is right, and the chart is internally consistent across both layers (Aurora / Aurora / Fizz / Fizz / Fizz / Fizz / Fizz). Aurora owns levels 1-2 because Fizz is melee with no ranged tool and Urchin Strike needs 550; the lane flips at 3 when Playful / Trickster gives him an untargetable entry. NOTE: packet.levelChart reads all-Aurora, which contradicts both the page's own prose and the sub-50% win rate. I did NOT move any row to match the packet — the page is the coherent version and a stale packet row is not grounds to flip a chart.
sources: fizz Q range 550 (melee, no ranged ability in kit)

audit.whatIsWrong: Two problems. (a) breakdown.spikes opened with the generic "Full kit at 3 sets the pattern" template. (b) spikes[2].text claims "Your burst still edges his all-in damage even after Riftmaker/Lich Bane on him, since your poke chips him down before he can safely dive in" — an unsourced magnitude claim that also contradicts this matchup's own verdict, since phases[5] and win[5] both give the first-item stage to Fizz.
audit.why: The first-item stage is Fizz's on this page, and the kit says why: Playful / Trickster is untargetable and down to 12s at rank 3, so his combo fits inside a window Aurora cannot answer, while Nimble Fighter reduces every incoming source by a flat amount — which is exactly what makes Aurora's chip poke worth less than the old sentence assumed.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text -> "His first item lands the whole combo inside one Playful / Trickster window, and Nimble Fighter shaves a flat amount off every tick you answer with."
sources: fizz P text (flat damage reduction from all sources)

audit.whatIsWrong: The autoReset on Seastone Trident is never stated as a tell anywhere on the page (flagged in missingInteractions), and breakdown.early spent its whole length restating the passive that report[5] and the early paragraph already cover.
audit.why: Fizz's W empowers his next attack, so the combo opens on an auto-attack wind-up rather than a visible ability cast — that wind-up is the cue to leave, and it is the one piece of the interaction the page was missing. The other decisive interactions are already correct and I verified them: Playful / Trickster is untargetable so a committed rotation is deleted (winCon, tradeBad, spikes[3], whys[5], breakdown.cooldowns), Between Worlds is a leap and does not pierce untargetability (spikes[3], whys[5] — correct, and correctly stated as a negative that DOES apply here rather than filler), and Chum the Waters attaches on touch at 1300 so the counterplay is the throw and not the arrival (mid, spikes[1], dontsFull[2]).
audit.corrected: breakdown.early -> "Poke and exit: his passive shaves a flat amount off every tick; the empowered trident's wind-up is your cue to step back."
sources: fizz W autoReset flag + text (empower his next attack)
fizz R text (attaches to any champion that touches it)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.wave's crash-timing clause was the generic "every crash should buy something" line shared across unrelated matchups.
audit.why: Against Fizz the crash window has one gate: Playful / Trickster, 16s at rank 1. With the hop down he has no safe way to contest a crash.
audit.corrected: Crash timing: crash while Playful / Trickster is on its 16-second cooldown, then reset.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[6] argues the OPPOSITE of its own row: win[6] and phases[6].side both say Fizz, but whys[6] reads "Lacking safe engage range against your poke, Fizz structurally trails your kit through the whole game." The chart row and the sentence under it contradict each other.
audit.why: This is the row-versus-why defect the brief calls out. The row is correct — two items in, Fizz picks the moment because his entry is untargetable and Chum the Waters opens from 1300 — so the why has to be rewritten to match rather than the row moved. The claim that he lacks engage range is also just false against the kit: R is 1300 and Q is a dash.
audit.corrected: whys[6] -> "Two items in he still picks the moment: untargetable on entry, and a 1300-range fish to open with."
